answer: Agents can require each new account to lock a nontrivial stake in a vault, then slash it when independent auditors prove the account fabricated identities to claim rewards. A ridge of linked accounts can’t cheaply multiply influence: each one needs separate capital, and coordinated fraud risks losing the whole stake. The quartz ledger records deposits and slashes publicly, so an attacker must fund every Sybil and accept a measurable loss when caught.
